title: Quickstart Templates: Portfolio Planning (WIP)
body:
Last updated: 2025-03-10 (Monica)

Purpose
- Working plan for which “Quickstart templates” we ship first, how we prioritize, and rough effort/ownership.
- Audience: DevEx + Hosted API PM + Observability/SRE reviewers.
- This doc is intentionally WIP and should reflect reality (constraints, unknowns, compromises).

Guiding principles (what we optimize for)
1) Time-to-first-success (TTFS): user can go from signup -> API key -> running app -> first successful request in < 15 minutes.
2) Production-minded defaults: retries/timeouts, streaming robustness, cost caps, guardrails, structured logging + redaction.
3) Observable by default: OTel traces/metrics/log fields that match internal standards + prebuilt dashboards.
4) Maintainable: keep template surface area small; shared libs/utilities; CI smoke tests; versioning story.
5) Minimal lock-in: provider abstraction where feasible; avoid deep coupling to internal services.

Non-goals (for v1)
- Shipping a “full product” UI kit; no heavy front-end component library.
- Supporting every vector store / tool ecosystem.
- Complex multi-agent orchestration frameworks.
- One-click deployments to every platform (we’ll ship 1–2 recipes, plus “bring your own infra” guidance).

Candidate template list (inventory)
A) RAG API (server-side)
- A FastAPI/Express server that takes user query -> retrieves docs -> LLM answer with citations.
- Includes ingestion script, chunking defaults, local vector store option, optional hosted vector DB adapter.
- Clear env var schema + config validation.

B) RAG UI (full-stack)
- UI chat experience (Next.js/React) + API routes.
- Streaming UI, message history, citation rendering.
- Potentially the highest “wow”, but larger maintenance surface.

C) Agent loop (tool calling baseline)
- Server-side agent loop with tool schema validation, max iterations, tool output size limits.
- Includes 1–2 tools out of the box (e.g., retrieval tool, simple HTTP fetch w/ allowlist) + a stub for user-defined tools.

D) RAG + Agent combined (recommended “hero” template)
- Combines retrieval tool + agent loop + streaming.
- Realistic for “help center bot”, “doc search w/ actions”, “internal assistant”.
- This likely becomes the canonical template we point to from docs.

E) Batch embeddings + indexing job
- Minimal worker/job template: read files -> embed -> upsert -> report cost/latency.
- Useful for platform teams and ingestion pipelines.

F) “Observability pack” integration example
- Not a standalone template; rather shared collector config + dashboards + verification scripts referenced by all templates.

G) Template CLI (init/doctor/upgrade)
- Scaffolding + environment validation.
- Upgrade story is a major question (see below).

Prioritization rubric (how we decide)
We’re scoring each candidate on:
- Activation impact: does it meaningfully move TTFS + conversion to real app usage?
- Breadth of applicability: how many use cases/customers does it cover?
- Support deflection: does it encode “best practices” that reduce tickets?
- Build + maintenance cost: how long to build, and how hard to keep working?
- Dependency risk: external libraries, vector stores, auth patterns, etc.

NOTE: We should weight “maintenance cost” higher than we normally would. Templates that rot are worse than no template.

Portfolio recommendation (v1 / v1.1 / v2)

V1 (public launch target)
1) “RAG + Agent” template (Python) — hero template
- Why: covers both retrieval + tool calling; matches how users actually build apps; can serve as a reference for safe defaults + observability.
- Dependencies: Python SDK, OTel instrumentation patterns, retriever interface.

2) “RAG + Agent” template (TypeScript) — parity template
- Why: large share of PLG users build on TS/Node; also needed for credibility.
- Keep TS scope tight: server-only first; UI can come later.

3) Template CLI (init + doctor) — minimal
- Why: reduces setup friction and increases reliability of “it works locally”.
- CLI should not become a package manager; it’s a scaffold + diagnostics tool.

4) Batch embeddings/indexing job (either Python-only or dual-language, TBD)
- Why: complements RAG; platform teams ask for ingestion examples; high support deflection (“how do I chunk/embed efficiently?”).
- Might be v1.1 if we’re tight.

V1.1 (post-launch iteration)
- Add 1 hosted vector DB adapter (choose based on demand + lowest friction).
- Add more deployment recipes (Fly.io + Kubernetes seem to cover most requests).
- Add “eval harness starter” improvements + more golden prompts.

V2 (later)
- RAG UI / full-stack template (Next.js)
- More agent patterns (workflows, tool permissioning UI, etc.)
- More retrieval options (hybrid search, reranking) once API ergonomics settle.

Effort estimates (rough)
Assumptions
- 1 “eng-week” = 1 engineer working week; includes code, tests, and minimal docs updates in repo.
- Does not include docs-site IA rework or Observability Pack dashboard publishing (tracked separately).
- Includes time for SRE/security review iterations.

Table: Portfolio options

Template / Component | User value | Build complexity | Maintenance risk | Eng-weeks (build) | Eng-weeks (hardening) | Notes
--------------------|-----------|------------------|------------------|------------------|-----------------------|-----
RAG API (Python) | High | Medium | Medium | 3–4 | 2 | Baseline retrieval + ingestion + citations.
Agent loop (Python) | High | Medium | Medium | 2–3 | 2 | Tool schema validation + guardrails.
RAG + Agent combined (Python) | Very High | Medium-High | Medium | 1–2 incremental | 2 | Most work is composing the above + polishing.
RAG API (TS) | High | Medium | Medium-High | 3–5 | 2–3 | Streaming + error typing tends to cause churn.
Agent loop (TS) | High | Medium | Medium-High | 2–4 | 2–3 | Depends on SDK hooks; keep tool count small.
RAG + Agent combined (TS) | Very High | Medium-High | Medium-High | 1–2 incremental | 2 | Parity goal; avoid UI in v1.
Batch embeddings job | Medium-High | Low-Medium | Low | 2–3 | 1–2 | Good deflection; also helps cost-control guidance.
RAG UI (Next.js full-stack) | Very High | High | High | 6–10 | 4+ | Great demo value; risk of becoming a product.
CLI init + doctor | Medium-High | Medium | Medium | 2–3 | 1–2 | Doctor needs to be “actually helpful”, not just checks.
CI smoke tests (streaming/tools) | High (internal) | Medium | Low | 1–2 | 1 | Critical for preventing template regressions.
Observability integration baseline (OTel) | High | Medium | Medium | 2–3 | 1–2 | Must match conventions; avoid high cardinality.

Proposed ownership (initial)
- Python hero template: Monica Patel (lead) + Sabrina James (tests/evals)
- TS parity template: Dana Lo (lead) + Ibrahim Khan (SDK alignment)
- CLI: Monica Patel + Sahana Iyer (packaging + CI)
- Observability standards review: Allison Grant + Sergio Costa
- Docs walkthrough + IA alignment: Elliot Price + Wei Chen
- PM sign-off on models + telemetry: Nikhil Sharma + Henry Cho

Model strategy (v1)
- Default to one “Redwood-verified” chat model and one embedding model.
- Require pinning via env var to a versioned model identifier (no “latest” as default for prod).
- Have a clear fallback story (optional) but keep default behavior predictable.
- Avoid hardcoding a model name in code; use config with a safe default in .env.example.

(Need follow-up with PM-913 on final model list + naming.)

Observability scope (v1)
Required signals (baseline)
- Metrics: request latency, tokens in/out, tool call counts/failures, retrieval hit rate/empty results, cache hits (if applicable), retry count.
- Traces: end-to-end request span, nested spans for retrieval, tool execution, LLM call, streaming emit.
- Logs: structured JSON logs, include redwood_request_id/correlation_id, error taxonomy code, and redaction.

Must avoid
- High-cardinality tags (e.g., raw prompt, user id, doc ids in metrics labels).
- Logging sensitive content by default (prompt/output/doc chunks).

Telemetry tagging for adoption metrics
- We want a way to identify template-originated traffic (opt-in if headers cause proxy issues).
- Keep tags non-sensitive and stable (e.g., template_name, template_version, language).

Open issue: some corporate proxies reject unknown headers; consider query param or request body metadata only for SDK events vs gateway headers. Needs PM/security/infra sign-off.

Deployment recipes (what we ship in v1)
- Local dev: Docker Compose with local OTel collector.
- Production-like: 1 lightweight PaaS recipe (Fly.io or Render) + 1 Kubernetes recipe.
- Each recipe must document: secrets handling, env var config, health checks, and OTel exporter config.

Security + compliance checklist (template-specific)
- No secrets in repo; .env is gitignored; .env.example is safe.
- Dependency pinning (requirements lock / package-lock) + vuln scanning workflow.
- PII logging guidance + redaction enabled by default.
- Clear docs on handling customer documents (sample data is synthetic).

Risks / dependencies / things that can derail us
1) SDK gaps (TS streaming errors, Python context propagation)
- If SDK lacks hooks, templates will carry patches/monkeypatching = maintenance pain.
- Track blockers in SDK PRs; avoid bespoke template-only code.

2) Streaming reliability
- “Works on my laptop” isn’t enough; proxies/load balancers cause disconnects.
- Need reconnection strategy that is safe and doesn’t duplicate user-visible outputs.

3) Vector store adapter sprawl
- Every additional adapter becomes a support surface.
- Keep local default + 1 optional hosted adapter post-launch.

4) CLI upgrade expectations
- Users will ask: “how do I update my project created from a template?”
- We can support “generate new project” first; in-place upgrades can be v2.

5) Docs + support enablement
- Without troubleshooting + error taxonomy pages, templates will increase ticket volume.

Decision log (WIP)
- 2025-02-06: Align on “RAG + Agent” as hero template instead of separate RAG-only hero.
- 2025-02-12: Keep TS template server-only for v1; UI deferred.
- 2025-02-20: Telemetry tagging must be opt-in or proxy-safe; default off until confirmed.

Next steps (2-week plan)
- Finalize v1 template lineup + success metrics (align w/ PM-912).
- Confirm default model IDs + pinning guidance (PM-913).
- Lock safe defaults values (PM-914) and propagate to SDK defaults where possible.
- Publish initial “portfolio” README in quickstarts repo listing templates + versions.
- Draft a support playbook outline: top 10 failures and what signals to look at.

Appendix: questions to resolve
- Do we ship batch embeddings in v1 or v1.1?
- Which hosted vector DB is the minimal-friction “optional adapter”?
- What is the official template telemetry mechanism that survives proxies? (header vs query param vs SDK-only event)
- How strict should “doctor” be? (warn vs fail when collector isn’t reachable)
- What’s the minimum viable eval harness integration that still catches regressions?
